analysis.title: Chat Recap 10/06/2026
key_insights: The authors say the market has crashed internally. NYSE new lows have exceeded new highs in every session since September 9th, about 18 straight sessions. On October 5th only 43% of S&P 500 names were above their 200-day average and 27% above their 50-day.

Breadth is starting to improve. NYSE new lows fell from 196 to 94 on October 5th and the McClellan oscillator rose from -43 to -7. New lows still beat new highs (net -53 vs -183 last week), which the authors call an early thaw, not a confirmed turn.

Confirmation test: NYSE new highs beating new lows for 3 or more straight sessions plus a McClellan oscillator cross above zero. If new lows re-accelerate above 300 for several sessions, the view is wrong.

Bottom line call: sell exposure to the S&P 500 and Nasdaq and buy the beaten-down, tax-loss part of the US equity market. The authors forecast a tax-loss selling climax within the next 30 days and a rotation from winners to losers over 30 to 120 days.

FactSet data as of September 28th: about 212 S&P 500 names (44% of the index) sit at least 20% below their 52-week highs, 17 are down 50% or more, and 63 of the 212 still carry buy ratings from at least 75% of analysts.

Market cap in Nasdaq 100 winners went from $30T in March to $40T and touched $43T this week. Total wealth went from $12T in Q4 2022 to $43T in Q4 2026. Most gains from SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic are still privately held.

Apple is flagged as the 'dumbest stock in the S&P 500'. It trades near $345 and briefly above $5T, at 37x earnings vs 21.5x for the S&P and about 10x sales vs a 3-5x 20-year average. The stated driver is memory cost inflation. The authors are long AAPD (an inverse Apple ETF) and a tax-loss basket on a 3-6 month view.

Memory cost data cited: DRAM is up roughly 260% y/y and NAND over 300%. Micron's 10-Q shows DRAM sales up 343% with bit shipments up about 20%. TrendForce projects 4Q26 DRAM contract prices up another 10-15% q/q and NAND up 15-20%.

TechInsights puts iPhone memory at about $39 for 12GB DRAM in the iPhone 17 Pro vs about $145 in the iPhone 18 Pro, and 256GB storage from $13 to $51. Memory goes from roughly 10% of bill of materials to about 34%, projected above 40% by 1H27. Apple guided gross margin to 46.5% from 48.1%, and the CFO said more than 100% of the decline is memory.
Early sell-side reports point to iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max US demand down low single digits y/y, with revenue for the first two months of the quarter tracking modestly below expectations.

Brazil is a long call via EWZ (long 2/3 in the authors' high conviction portfolio). EWZ is +37% in 2026 and +48% over one year vs QQQ +23%/+25%. The Brazil first round gave Flavio Bolsonaro 47% vs Lula 41%, the Ibovespa jumped 4.9% (most since 2022) and runoff odds for Bolsonaro rose from 60% to 84%.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 133 bps from a February 2026 low of 3.95% to a September high of 5.29%, nearly matching the roughly 137 bp rise in the 2013 Taper Tantrum (Goldman). Bloomberg commentary says the September weak payroll print looks less convincing as a labor-market break given ISM employment turning to expansion and S&P Global showing the strongest job creation since June 2022.

Reasons cited for the bond selloff: Trump diesel tax relief (up to about $25B a year), European sovereign risk (French national strike on November 5, Spanish snap elections on November 29), and curve steepening after last week's Fed dovish pivot. 2s30s broke back above its downtrend line with RSI jumping from about 20 to about 58.
US September ISM Services fell to 54.9 from 55.4 vs 55 estimate. Final S&P Global composite PMI was 58.4. A source argues the yield rally is driven by US growth strength.

Equity tape: Nasdaq-100 hit a new all-time high with NQ near 31,500, Nvidia took out its May 14th high, and the SOX is at its upper Bollinger band. The S&P 500 is testing its upper Bollinger band, which has narrowed since August. Only 44% of large-cap active funds beat benchmarks in September and the cap-weighted S&P beat equal-weight by nearly 5 points (BofA).

Options flow: Citi says S&P 500 option volume is 14% above its 12-month average, with 0DTE at 66% of activity and 0DTE calls outnumbering puts in nine of the past 11 sessions. A 77k IEF Oct 9 88.5 put block traded at $0.17.

Russell 2000 refinancing risk: more than 40% of Russell 2000 debt is short-term or floating rate. CMBS delinquency rose 17 bps to 8.02% (Trepp), and close to $1T of refinancing is due over 12-24 months.
Credit desk color: CDX IG tightened to 59.75, with systematic protection buyers mostly in HY. Credit is moving wider on equity strength.

Energy and commodities: the diesel crack spread has fallen sharply from a September peak near 345, Brent bounced off its uptrend line, and natural gas settled at $3.066/mmbtu (+1%). Raw sugar futures are up about 20% in 5 sessions to a 52-week high, driven by the Brazil election result. Saudi Arabia cut its Asia benchmark crude price to a 6-year low.

Crypto and Bitcoin treasury: Strategy (MSTR) sold 92,894 shares for $15.70M net during Oct 1-4 to fund bitcoin purchases. The CFTC chair said the CFTC is proposing its first round of crypto market regulation. Citrini is reported long Bitcoin via IBIT.

M&A announced: Schneider Electric to buy PTC for $205/share ($23.7B EV), CH Robinson to buy RXO ($5.8B), CVE to buy Athabasca Oil ($5.7B EV), Nippon Paint to buy Akzo Nobel's Southeast Asia decorative paints business ($1.35B), WMS to buy StormTrap ($530MM).

Political and AI-capex risk: Texas Governor odds show Abbott at 73% (from 93% in July). Democrat Hinojosa has threatened a data-center moratorium and Texas is the major outlier in planned data-center capacity. The AOC 2028 Polymarket contract is at 15.7 cents.

Yen is described as in a long-term bear market per a multi-year head and shoulders. Japanese investors are selling foreign bonds including French government bonds and buying foreign equities and unwinding yen carry trades.

risk_factors: Breadth could re-deteriorate if NYSE new lows re-accelerate above 300 for several sessions.
Rising long-end yields with the 10-year above long-term resistance, and a growing budget deficit from tax relief measures.
European sovereign risk in France and Spain, including Japanese selling of French bonds.
Russell 2000 floating-rate and near-term refinancing exposure, plus CMBS delinquencies and roughly $1T of refinancing due in 12-24 months.
Memory price inflation squeezing Apple and consumer names.
Texas data-center moratorium risk if Hinojosa wins, and a 2028 left-leaning election scenario that could hit both bonds and stocks.
Brazil's next president may not deliver the fiscal fixes investors expect.
Mega-cap momentum concentration, with market leadership narrowed toward megacaps.
charts_described: The 2s30s spread rebounded sharply from its late-September low and broke back above its downtrend line, with RSI jumping from about 20 to about 58.
The 10-year yield has held above its long-term upward-sloping resistance line over a few sessions.
Nasdaq-100 pushed through resistance from the early June high to a new all-time high, with MACD above its signal line but well below its May peak.
The S&P 500 bounced back above its 20-day moving average and is testing the upper Bollinger band, with the bands narrowed since August.
The diesel crack spread has fallen sharply from a September peak near 345.
Raw sugar futures broke above their September highs to a new 52-week high, up about 56% since the June low.
The High Yield ETF is oversold but faded an obvious resistance line and remains above its March 27th low.
vol_and_positioning: Today's implied moves: SPY 50 bps, QQQ 75 bps, IWM 68 bps, IBIT 119 bps, TLT 76 bps. ES implied move is plus or minus 39 handles, with ES range 7738 to 7816 around 7777.

Key ES watch level is 7754. Dealers hold strong positive gamma at SPX 7700. The -1.0x implied level of ES 7738 equals SPX 7684, where vol sellers would use SPX Oct 5 7680 puts. Vol sellers are expected at SPX 7765 and 7770 calls near the top of the range.
Citi says S&P 500 option volume is 14% above its 12-month average, with 0DTE at 66% of activity and calls outnumbering puts in nine of the past 11 sessions.
A 77k block of IEF Oct 9 88.5 puts traded at $0.17 (about 29 delta), equal to 2.2 million IEF shares for sale.
Hedge funds are said to have started making money on the 2s30s steepener. Yen positioning has been flip-flopping.
Many hedge fund styles were long high-momentum and short low-momentum equities, a crowding that peaked in the last week of June.
Systematic protection buyers were seen in HY credit. NYSE ticks closed at -582.
geopolitical: Brazil first-round presidential election gave Flavio Bolsonaro 47% and Lula 41%. Runoff odds for Bolsonaro rose from 60% to 84%.
Spain PM called snap elections for November 29 after a key housing vote failed.
French unions called a national strike for November 5, and large protests are scheduled for teachers and Paris public transport.
Yemeni forces, backed by Saudi Arabia, retook Mocha city from the Houthis, backed by Iran. Saudi Arabia is planning an offensive to retake the Red Sea shipping lane.
Iran's oil minister resigned as a US blockade cripples the energy industry. Reuters said Middle East exports in late September rose above pre-war levels.
Berlin and Paris are floating a trade tool to cut China's access to the EU market.
US midterm elections and 2028 election odds are discussed, including the AOC 2028 contract at 15.7 cents on Polymarket.
Texas governor race has Abbott at 73% odds, down from 93% in July, with data-center moratorium risk from challenger Hinojosa.
cross_bank_references: Goldman compares the current 10Y rise of about 133 bps to the 2013 Taper Tantrum rise of about 137 bps.
Citi says S&P 500 option volume is 14% above its 12-month average with 0DTE at 66% of activity.
BofA says just 44% of large-cap active funds beat their benchmarks in September.
Citadel Securities says the Treasury selloff reflects stronger US growth and competition for capital rather than rising inflation concerns.
